# agent-detect

> agent-detect infers the current AI agent's harness, provider, and model — multi-harness, multi-OS,
> multi-arch — so AI agents can identify themselves accurately, as required by various AI policies
> and skills. This site is the browsable registry of its rule tables and fixture-verified results:
> which harness × provider × model combos are known, whether each is reciprocal, and the exact
> identify / trailer / explain outputs the CLI produces for them.

The detection tool itself is a prebuilt zig binary (no npm/crates package) with zero required
runtime dependencies and no network I/O at detection time:
https://github.com/bevry-vibes/agent-detect

## how the site is organised

`/` is a single-page app. Three searchable dropdowns (harness, provider, model) plus a free-text
search box filter a results table; clicking a row opens that combo's full-page results view —
`identify`, `trailer co-author`, `trailer assisted-by`, and `explain` (plus `found`/`raw`,
`check-reciprocal`, stderr lines, and capture meta when recorded) — tabbed per platform and channel
(`captured` = live fixture, `declared` = declared fixture), sorted latest-generated first. Each
block carries copy + copy-command buttons for the CLI invocation behind it. The results table keeps
every row in the DOM with CSS `content-visibility: auto`, so native Ctrl/Cmd+F searches the whole
list.

URL query params mirror the CLI's `--harness= / --provider= / --model=` flags: display names,
labels, and aliases are accepted, and the URL is canonicalised to the strict-slug alphanumeric ids
("Kimi Code" and "kimi-code" land as `kimicode`). `?search=` free-text matches combo ids and
harness/provider/model names and ids (substring, case-insensitive). `?agent=<agent_id>` is the
agent results page — a full-page replacement of the index (not a modal); `?platform=<platform>`
pins a fixture tab (the default is the latest-generated fixture; clicking it again clears the
param). The site header wordmark or the page's "back to results" button returns to the index with
the scroll position restored. All navigation uses the HTML5 history API
(pushState/replaceState/popstate).

## endpoints

- `/` — the app (hero, filters, results table, detail panel)
- `/index.json` — JSON results. Accepts `?harness=&provider=&model=&search=&agent=&platform=` with
  the same name→id resolution on the dims. Unfiltered it returns the compact combo index; with any
  filter it embeds each matching combo's full fixtures (identify + both trailers + explain + meta),
  capped at 50 combos before degrading to compact rows with `"truncated": true`.
- `/identify/<agent_id>.json` — one combo's merged result: every platform × channel fixture with its
  verbatim outputs and meta. agent_id is the dash-joined strict slugs, e.g.
  `cline-clinepass-deepseekv4flash`.
- `/registry.json` — the rule registry: harnesses, providers, models with policy fields (training
  postures, openness, licenses, scandal flags) and their source URLs.
- `/data/combos.json` — the compact combo index (the same rows the table renders).
- `/data/agents/<agent_id>.json` — the same bytes as `/identify/<agent_id>.json`.
- `/llms.txt` — this file.

## notes for agents

- ids are strict slugs: lowercase alphanumeric with all separators stripped
  (`kimi-code` → `kimicode`, `qwen3.8-27b` → `qwen3827b`); agent_id joins the three dims with dashes
  (`cline-clinepass-deepseekv4flash`), and doubles as the trailer email local part
  (`<agent_id@local>`).
- `reciprocal: true` means the combo passes agent-detect's reciprocity requirement (per the policy
  documented in the upstream repo); `explain.state` is the detailed state
  (`reciprocal | not-reciprocal | unknown | undetectable`).
- combos listed in the registry dropdowns but absent from `/index.json` results are registry rules
  with no fixture yet — verify them live with
  `agent-detect check-reciprocal --harness=<id> --provider=<id> --model=<id>`.
- data is regenerated from the upstream repo's committed fixture channels on every deploy; the site
  stores nothing and reads nothing from visitors.
